title: Check SMALLS System Health Using the Smalls Overview HMI Screen (Color-Coded Layout)
summary: Use the SMALLS overview screen on the System HMI to quickly identify which parts of the SMALLS system are in a normal vs abnormal (color-coded) status based on the system layout.
when_to_use: When you need a fast, at-a-glance health check of the SMALLS system parts using the color-coded SMALLS system layout.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Open the System HMI SMALLS overview screen and identify any parts showing abnormal color-coded status; stop/escalate when abnormal indications are widespread or unclear.
access_or_tools_needed: Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU (System HMI access where the SMALLS button is available)

access_required: System HMI access where the SMALLS button is available (Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU)

visual_references.description: Figure 4-4: Smalls System Overview Screen (color-coded SMALLS system layout).

steps.title: Open the "Smalls" overview screen from the System HMI
steps.purpose: Get to the SMALLS overview layout that shows color-coded status for each part.
steps.instruction: On the System HMI, press the SMALLS button to open the "Smalls" overview screen.
steps.healthy_condition: The "Smalls" overview screen loads successfully and shows the SMALLS system layout.
steps.failure_condition: The "Smalls" overview screen does not open or the SMALLS layout is not visible.

actions.label: Press SMALLS
actions.exact_action: Press SMALLS to access the "Smalls" overview screen.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access the "Smalls" overview screen, stop and escalate for support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Press SMALLS to access the "Smalls" overview screen. The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

steps.title: Review the SMALLS system layout on the "Smalls" overview screen
steps.purpose: Identify each SMALLS part shown on the layout so you can check its color-coded status.
steps.instruction: On the "Smalls" overview screen, review the SMALLS system layout.
steps.expected_result: You can see the SMALLS system layout with parts displayed for status checking.
steps.healthy_condition: The layout is fully visible and each part is present on the screen for color inspection.
steps.failure_condition: Parts are missing/unreadable on the layout, or the screen does not provide a clear view of the layout.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot clearly determine which parts are shown on the layout, stop and escalate.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

steps.title: Check each SMALLS part’s color-coded status indicator
steps.purpose: Determine which parts are abnormal by observing the color-coded status indicators on the layout.
steps.instruction: For each part shown on the layout, observe the color-coded status indicator.
steps.expected_result: You have identified which parts (if any) show abnormal color-coded status (i.e., not the normal/expected color for that part).
steps.healthy_condition: All parts show the normal/expected color-coded status indicators for their respective parts.
steps.failure_condition: One or more parts show abnormal color-coded status indicators.

actions.label: Observe color-coded indicators
actions.exact_action: Observe the color-coded status of each part of the system.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if multiple system parts show abnormal color-coded status.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

steps.title: Identify abnormal parts and decide whether to stop/escalate
steps.purpose: Ensure abnormal indications are handled appropriately and escalate when abnormality is widespread or unclear.
steps.instruction: Identify any parts whose color-coded status indicates an abnormal condition (i.e., not the normal/expected color for that part). If the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, treat it as abnormal.
steps.expected_result: You have a clear list of abnormal parts (if any) and a decision to escalate when abnormality is widespread or unclear.
steps.healthy_condition: No parts indicate abnormal color-coded status; no offline/blocked section is indicated.
steps.failure_condition: Multiple parts show abnormal color-coded status, or the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, or you cannot determine which parts are abnormal.

actions.label: Identify abnormal parts
actions.exact_action: Identify any parts whose color-coded status indicates an abnormal condition.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if multiple system parts show abnormal color-coded status.
Stop and escalate if the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action.
Stop and escalate if you cannot determine which parts are abnormal from the screen.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

success_criteria: Operator can open the "Smalls" overview screen and visually identify abnormal color-coded status indicators for any SMALLS parts.
Operator escalates when multiple parts show abnormal color-coded status or when abnormality is unclear.
healthy_conditions: All parts on the "Smalls" overview screen show normal/expected color-coded status indicators.
No offline/blocked section is indicated on the SMALLS layout.
failure_conditions: One or more SMALLS parts show abnormal color-coded status indicators.
Multiple SMALLS parts show abnormal color-coded status indicators.
The operator cannot determine which parts are abnormal from the screen.
The layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action.
escalation_guidance: If multiple parts show abnormal color-coded status, or if the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, stop and escalate for support.

missing_details: The manual section provided does not define the specific color-to-meaning mapping (what each color corresponds to). This runbook therefore instructs the operator to treat any color that is not the normal/expected color for that part as abnormal, without specifying exact meanings.
